question: How much did Mindgard raise in its latest funding round?

hits.title: Mindgard Raises $30M Series A - Mindgard
hits.snippet: BOSTON, Mass., Aug 12, 2026 – Mindgard, the leader in AI security, announced today that it has closed a $30 million Series A financing led by Album VC with participation from Karma Ventures and existing investors .406 Ventures, Atlantic Bridge, IQ Capital, and Lakestar. Mindgard plans to use the funding to scale the company across product, engineering, sales, and marketing in response to significant customer demand.

hits.title: Lancaster University spinout Mindgard lands $30M after breaking Cursor, ChatGPT, and Google's AI guardrails — TFN
hits.snippet: - Mindgard has raised $30 million in Series A funding, bringing its total funding to almost $42 million. - The platform has found more than 150 vulnerabilities in AI products, including a zero-day in Cursor and weaknesses in ChatGPT’s guardrails. - Two major competitors were acquired in the past year, and the AI security market is expected to reach $56.5 billion by 2033. ... The startup completed a $30 million Series A round led by Album VC, with new investor Karma Ventures and returning investors .406 Ventures, Atlantic Bridge, IQ Capital, and Lakestar. This brings its total funding to nearly $42 million, up from about $11.9 million raised in a 2023 seed round and a December 2024 Series A tranche.

hits.title: Mindgard Raises $30 Million to Protect AI Systems - SecurityWeek
hits.snippet: AI security startup Mindgard today announced raising $30 million in a Series A funding round that brings the total raised by the company close to $42 million.

hits.title: Mindgard raises £22m Series A as AI security funding matures | TechMarketView
hits.snippet: London and Boston-based Mindgard has raised $30m (£22m) in Series A funding led by Album VC, with participation from existing backers including .406 Ventures and IQ Capital. The round is a substantial step up from previous raises (see - Mindgard raises further $8m for AI security testing), and comes roughly two years after the company was spun out of Lancaster University with £3m in seed funding (see - Mindgard raises £3m for securing AI models).
